theme: Three て-form helper verbs — ～ておく (in advance), ～てしまう (oops / all done), ～てみる (give it a try)
intro: Once you know the て-form, bolt on these three helpers to add a shade of meaning — preparation, completion, or a low-pressure try.

grammar.title: Three て-form helpers

rules.label: ～ておく
rules.detail: do something in advance / leave it set up and ready; casual → ～とく
examples: 予約する → 予約しておく (book it ahead of time)

rules.label: ～てしまう
rules.detail: finish completely, or do it by accident / regrettably; casual → ～ちゃう／～じゃう
examples: 食べる → 食べてしまう (eat it all up / eat it, oops)

rules.label: ～てみる
rules.detail: try doing something to see how it goes; conjugates like the verb みる
examples: 食べる → 食べてみる (try eating it)

grammar.bigPoint: All three attach to the て-form you already drill — the て-form does the heavy lifting; just add the helper.

vocab.jp: 準備する（じゅんびする）
注文する（ちゅうもんする）

examples.jp: ホテルを予約しておきました。
examples.en: I booked the hotel in advance.

examples.jp: 新しいラーメン屋で注文してみます。
examples.romaji: Atarashii raamen-ya de chuumon shite mimasu.
examples.en: I'll try ordering at the new ramen place.

examples.jp: 電車に傘を忘れてしまいました。
examples.romaji: Densha ni kasa o wasurete shimaimashita.
examples.en: I unfortunately left my umbrella on the train.

note: ～ておく = preparation ('get it done ahead'); ～てしまう = completion or an 'oops'; ～てみる = a low-pressure 'let me try'. In speech you'll hear the contractions constantly: 調べとくね (I'll look it up), やっちゃった! (oops, I did it!).

selfCheck.q: How would you say 'I want to try looking it up'? (Build it from 調べる + ～てみる + ～たい.)
selfCheck.a: 調べてみたいです。(Shirabete mitai desu.) — 調べる → 調べて, add みる → みたい: 調べて + みたい + です.
